transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because my sleep has just been broken for a really long time now. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I end up waking up to every little sound in the house. And after all that, I'm always up before my alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
When you're lying in bed trying to fall asleep, do you find yourself worrying or having racing thoughts that keep you awake?

No, not really. My mind doesn't really race or anything like that. Honestly, I'm usually so exhausted by the time I get to bed that falling asleep isn't the problem. I drop off pretty quick. It's just... I can't stay asleep once I do. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm lying there worrying.
When you wake up in the morning, how is your mood? Do you find yourself feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, especially in those early morning hours?

Yeah, I do feel pretty down. Most days, it just feels like... well, like the color has completely gone out of things. It's not just in the early morning, either. Even when I'm sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or looking at art I used to really enjoy, it all just feels flat. I actually find myself having to work hard not to tear up sometimes, and there's no clear reason for it. I just feel sad.
How long have you been feeling this way—this sadness and flatness along with the sleep problems? Has it been going on for a few weeks, or longer?

It's definitely been longer than a few weeks. Actually, um... this has all been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us. That was a little over two years ago now. So, yeah, it's been quite a while.
You mentioned that art you used to enjoy now feels flat. Besides that, are there other activities or hobbies that you used to find pleasure in that no longer interest you or bring you joy?

No, not really. I mean... I don't have a lot of other hobbies to begin with. Between my job and everything at home, I never really had the time for much else anyway. So, um, no, I haven't really noticed losing interest in anything else, just because there wasn't much else I did for fun besides looking at my art books.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past two years? And separately, how is your energy level during the day—do you feel fatigued or exhausted even when you've rested?

Well, I don't really have much of an appetite anymore. I just... I end up picking at whatever I make for everyone else at the house. Or, um, I'll just grab a piece of toast after my shift. I haven't been trying to lose weight at all, but my clothes have definitely been hanging a lot looser on me lately. 

As for my energy... I don't know, I guess I just don't have a lot of it between work and everything going on at home.

Beyond the sleep troubles and low mood you've described, do you find yourself worrying excessively about things—like your job, your health, finances, or family matters—even when there's no immediate reason to worry?

No, I wouldn't say I do. I mean... obviously there's regular stress with my mother-in-law being in the house and the demands of my job, but I don't really sit around worrying about things for no reason. It's not an anxious feeling. I'm just... tired and flat, like I said. So, no, I haven't really noticed any excessive worry like that.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.9 (Anxiety Disorder, unspecified). Patient explicitly denies excessive worry, racing thoughts, and anxious feelings. The clinical picture is consistent with Major Depressive Disorder: persistent depressed mood for 2+ years, anhedonia (loss of pleasure in art), sleep disturbance (early morning awakening pattern), appetite/weight loss, fatigue, and no significant anxiety symptoms. This is a clear depressive episode.
